title: Anthropic's Possible $100B IPO, Nvidia's $7B Poolside Bet, and California's AI-Firing Ban
sources: The Neuron, The Rundown AI, Morning Brew, 1440 Daily Digest (Aug 24)
tldr: Anthropic's bankers reportedly say its IPO could raise over $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, potentially the largest stock debut ever.
Nvidia is paying $7 billion to build a US rival to Chinese open-weight models, even as it raises AI chip prices more than 15%.
California revived a bill banning employers from letting AI fire or discipline workers without human sign-off.

tips.heading: Make AI prove its homework before you publish its draft
steps: Ask it to list every factual claim, number, quote, and named source in the draft, quoting the exact source language so you can Ctrl/Cmd+F it.
Open every source yourself and confirm it actually supports the claim; rewrite or delete anything that doesn't check out.
Never ask AI to "repair" an invented citation — start over from a real source.
tips.prompt: Audit this draft for factual risk. List every claim, number, quote, and named source I must verify manually. Give only URLs already present in the draft. Mark anything unsupported as DO NOT PUBLISH. Do not invent or repair sources.

tips.heading: Turn any spreadsheet into a shareable dashboard with Gemini Canvas
steps: Open your spreadsheet in Google Sheets, launch Gemini in a new tab, click +, and select Canvas.
Prompt it to build the dashboard from your data, then copy the Canvas link to view or share it outside the chat.
Keep refining by talking to Gemini in the chat — anyone with the link sees your updates live.
Ask Gemini to turn the same tabs into slides, then export to Google Slides or PDF.
tips.prompt: Make me an interactive dashboard using the data from tabs one and two

news.body: Anthropic's IPO could be the largest stock market debut ever. Bankers reportedly told investors the company could raise more than $100 billion, pushing its valuation to nearly $2 trillion, more than double its $965 billion private-round valuation in June. A listing could come as soon as October, with Anthropic beating OpenAI (which isn't planning to list until 2027) to public markets.
news.means: If this holds, Anthropic becomes only the fourth company ever to cross a $2 trillion valuation, alongside Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia. Worth tracking closely if any client work touches Claude, Anthropic partnerships, or competitive positioning against OpenAI.

news.body: California lawmakers revived a bill banning AI from firing or disciplining workers without human sign-off. The "No Robo Bosses Act" (SB 947) follows Governor Newsom's veto of an earlier version last October; a widely cited example involves an AI agent that recommended firing a worker based on a policy it had itself written and then "forgot."
news.means: A concrete signal for any client using or considering AI in HR/people-ops decisions — build a human-sign-off step into any AI-assisted disciplinary or termination workflow now, before more states follow California's lead.

news.body: Nvidia is spending big to build a US rival to Chinese open-weight AI models, while also raising its own chip prices. It's paying $6 billion to license AI startup Poolside's technology and hire its engineers, plus investing $1 billion more at a $12 billion valuation. Separately, Nvidia is raising prices on its next-generation Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips by 15-17% starting early next year, adding roughly $5 billion to the cost of a single large data center.
news.means: Budget accordingly if any client's roadmap depends on next-gen Nvidia hardware — a 15-17% price hike on flagship chips will ripple into AI infrastructure costs across the board.

beyond_ai.body: US-Canada trade talks collapsed and new 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods took effect Friday. The tariffs hit forestry, alcohol, dairy, and textiles (even hockey sticks and dog leashes); Canada's PM Mark Carney vowed dollar-for-dollar retaliation effective September 8, saying "you're at war when you get attacked... we got attacked." Trump responded on Truth Social that "Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one."
beyond_ai.angle: Directly relevant for clients with cross-border supply chains — this moved from talks collapsing to tariffs actually in effect, with a firm retaliation date now on the calendar.
beyond_ai.starter: With Canada's retaliatory tariffs set for September 8, have we mapped which of our clients' supply chains are exposed?

beyond_ai.body: A humanoid robot broke Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record at China's World Humanoid Robot Games, then crashed into a wall. Reports differ on the details: 1440 puts an unnamed robot at 9.39 seconds, while Morning Brew names the robot "Lightning," built by smartphone maker Honor, at 9.32 seconds — both faster than Bolt's 9.58-second record. The Games feature over 2,000 humanoid robots, days after the US banned imports of foreign-made humanoid robots over national-security concerns.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only — though worth knowing if any client touches robotics, manufacturing automation, or is affected by the new US import ban.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you see the robot that broke Usain Bolt's speed record this weekend, then ran straight into a wall?

beyond_ai.body: The federal government unveiled a new 10-year Colorado River water-management plan after years of drought left Lake Mead and Lake Powell at record lows. California must cut water use 10%, Nevada 16%, and Arizona 27%; upstream states face no cuts yet, and lawsuits between states are possible.
beyond_ai.angle: Directly relevant if any client operates data centers, agriculture, or real estate development in the Southwest — water is becoming a hard constraint on growth there, AI data centers included.
beyond_ai.starter: Has anyone modeled what a 27% water-use cut means for growth plans in Arizona?

beyond_ai.body: Paramount Skydance and California's attorney general were set to discuss settling an antitrust case over Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, brought by 12 state AGs. California wants "robust structural remedies"; pressure is mounting from the governor and the Directors Guild to resolve it.
beyond_ai.angle: Directly relevant if you advise media or entertainment clients — a live example of how far state AGs can push on merger conditions even after a deal closes.
beyond_ai.starter: If a client's merger closed and a state AG still wanted structural remedies after the fact, how would we advise them to respond?

beyond_ai.body: Harvard Business School is charging $699 for an entrepreneur bootcamp that includes AI avatars of its professors, which listen to pitches and give feedback.
beyond_ai.angle: Directly relevant — AI-driven training products are already commanding premium pricing; worth benchmarking against any learning and development work in our own pipeline.
beyond_ai.starter: Would our clients pay a premium for an AI-avatar version of our own training content, the way Harvard just did?
